content.text: The adapter has two resilience paths that merit closer inspection: snapshot polling under slow responses and the lifetime of cached Booklet failures. I’m checking their effects against the surrounding monitor code.

{
  "role": "slop-review",
  "head": "60df907d432078e0edbda71568becdb5af6cd193",
  "base": "ad92a0864ac56987a4896fd5770abab0c0c9b271",
  "verdict": "request_changes",
  "signal": "high",
  "summary": "The port has substantive resilience and navigation defects in the native Monitor adapter. The supplied evidence supports the stated local validation, but does not establish CI qualification for this HEAD.",
  "findings": [
    {
      "severity": "medium",
      "path": "rewrite-app/apps/web/src/app/native-monitor/group-monitor/backend.service.ts",
      "line": 17,
      "title": "Polling cancels every snapshot that takes longer than five seconds",
      "evidence": "The five-second timer uses switchMap, whose teardown aborts the previous request. If snapshot responses consistently take over five seconds, none can complete, despite the HTTP client's 20-second deadline. Cancellation also bypasses the error display, leaving the monitor without fresh data or a useful failure indication.",
      "recommendation": "Allow an in-flight poll to finish or reach its existing deadline before starting the next one, and report timeout failures. Add a focused slow-response test."
    },
    {
      "severity": "medium",
      "path": "rewrite-app/apps/web/src/app/native-monitor/group-monitor/booklet/booklet.service.ts",
      "line": 36,
      "title": "A transient Booklet failure is cached for the entire access session",
      "evidence": "The backend converts network and server failures into BookletError values, which shareReplay retains in the name-keyed cache. Subsequent snapshots reuse that completed error instead of retrying, so a temporary failure leaves Booklet-dependent display and controls unavailable until the access identity changes or the page is reloaded. The same pattern exists in Original, but the port exposes the defect in the new monitor.",
      "recommendation": "Evict or retry failed Booklet results while retaining successful caching and access-scope isolation; cover recovery after a transient failure."
    },
    {
      "severity": "medium",
      "path": "rewrite-app/apps/web/src/app/native-monitor/group-monitor/group-monitor.component.ts",
      "line": 289,
      "title": "Finish-all navigates to an Original route absent from the rewrite",
      "evidence": "After the confirmed finish-all command succeeds, the port navigates to /r/starter. The rewrite has no such route; its wildcard redirects to home, ejecting the operator from the native Monitor flow while the native session remains active.",
      "recommendation": "Navigate to the intended rewrite Monitor destination and define the desired session lifecycle after finishing. Verify the confirmed finish-all flow in the native UI."
    }
  ],
  "verified": [
    "Confirmed the worktree HEAD and inspected the committed diff, native transport and session adapters, Monitor lifecycle, cache, routes, smoke script, and relevant Original source.",
    "Read both supplied evidence files: the cache proof reports reproduction of the old failure and a 12-marker positive browser pass using the configured cache.",
    "The supplied validation record reports a 468.49 kB initial production bundle against the unchanged 470 kB limit, and explicitly identifies the earlier 5d9 CI failure."
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "This was a read-only source review; supplied broad build and test results were not rerun.",
    "The reported findings are derived from source inspection and were not independently reproduced in a browser.",
    "The supplied evidence does not show that HEAD has passed CI, and the review does not establish visual parity or completion of the explicitly deferred native transport and participant work."
  ]
}
